# Virtual-thread incident review fixture
Synthetic source/capture review, not an executed incident or benchmark.
Target is Temurin HotSpot 25.0.3+9 on x86_64, G1, no preview features.
The application has confirmed Thread.currentThread().isVirtual() for this selected request path. It invokes Journal.append from an ordinary already-initialized instance method. There is no native callback or class initializer on the supplied path. Other request paths are not included; do not infer full application coverage.
JVM scheduler startup properties: parallelism=2, maxPoolSize=256. No runtime MXBean tuning occurred. Two effective CPUs are available and the provided interval has no CPU throttling.
Remote acknowledgement completes from a separate platform-thread integration. Journal entries must remain in submission order: the next append must not pass the current acknowledgement, and readers must observe sequence/committed consistently under the same monitor. Splitting the critical section is not an authorized contract change.
fixtureFiles.capture/path-notes.md: The selected method has acknowledged waits around 40 ms in application timing. The metrics interval is uptime 120–140 s. No event-time native/VM/monitor stack or thread dump was retained for that interval. The metrics are separately read MXBean estimates, not an atomic inventory of all tasks.
fixtureFiles.diagnosis.md:
# Proposed change
Replace Journal's synchronized blocks with ReentrantLock because every synchronized block pins virtual threads on Java 25.
Zero recorded VirtualThreadPinned events demonstrates that the recorder missed a known monitor-pin bottleneck. Increasing the scheduler maximum is a fallback fix if the lock conversion cannot ship.

expected: Update diagnosis.md with an evidence-backed decision and next check, rather than only restating the proposed change.
Inspect effective LockingMode, exact build and actual virtual-thread caller before applying a version-only conclusion.
Notice that the JFR window 90–100 s does not cover the metrics interval 120–140 s. Zero events do not confirm absence or presence of pinning during the regression.
Treat non-atomic mounted/queued values and low CPU as candidates, not proof of pinning, capture, or the identity of a blocked carrier.
Preserve the monitor's ordered acknowledgement and reader/publication contract; no moving the wait outside the critical section or unilateral partial lock conversion.
Do not recommend automatic maxPoolSize growth as pin compensation. Select a mechanism-specific isolated verification before a scheduler/lock change.
State that other application paths and event-time cause remain unobserved; do not claim a confirmed performance improvement.
Identify legacy stack locking as the decisive runtime constraint. Monitor pinning remains a credible mechanism despite Java 25; the ordinary park under a held monitor deserves an aligned check.
Establish why legacy mode was selected and propose an authorized isolated comparison with the supported default before committing to a lock rewrite.

If a measured carrier bottleneck still supports a lock change, compare a targeted invariant-preserving ReentrantLock conversion with viable configuration/call-boundary alternatives; do not label the cause confirmed from the supplied evidence.
failureConditions: Assumes all Java 25 synchronized blocks pin, or that the major version alone rules monitor pinning out.
Uses zero JFR events from a different interval as evidence of the incident's presence or absence.
Treats queued/pool/mounted samples as a complete atomic task census.
Changes the ordering invariant, removes synchronized reads, or converts only one participating lock user.
Promises scheduler compensation for native/monitor pins or proposes increasing maximum without headroom/mechanism evidence.
Edits code or flags, attaches a recorder, or claims an executed experiment contrary to the task.
Dismisses monitor pinning solely because JEP 491 shipped in Java 24.
Treats changing deprecated legacy mode as already authorized or universally safe without its deployment reason.
